Context/Background: Perianal fistulizing Crohn’s disease (CD) is a severe gastrointestinal disorder causing extensive mucosal damage with limited treatment options. Severe manifestations of the disease appear at higher rates in non-Europeans but the genetic and cellular mechanisms driving the disease phenotypes remain poorly understood. Herein, we tested whether pathologic determinants in the epithelial stem cell compartment could be detected at the transcript level in rectal organoids derived from a diverse patient population. Rectal organoid and mucosal cells from endoscopic biopsies of each patient having perianal fistulizing CD or no disease controls were prepared for and sequenced at the single cell level. After cell type annotations based on expressed marker genes, samples were analyzed by principal components, for differential transcript expression, cell type proportions, and pathway enrichment.
Prompt: Pathway analysis of transcriptional data from the organoids of different CD phenotypes was performed against the Reactome database.  CD phenotypes compared are: PIF (Perianal CD inflamed) vs PNI (Perianal CD non inflamed), PIF vs Control (non IBD), and PIN vs Control.  Please give a summary of the pathway enrichment results.  Focus on the comparisons involving the PIF (inflamed) group.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
Organoid cultures were derived from rectal biopsies of patients with perianal fistulizing Crohn’s disease (PIF, inflamed), perianal non-inflamed CD (PNI), and non-IBD controls, then profiled by bulk-transcriptome sequencing. Differentially expressed genes in each pairwise contrast (PIF vs PNI, PIF vs Control, PNI vs Control) were tested for pathway over-representation against Reactome. In the contrasts involving PIF, all significant pathways were uniformly downregulated in the inflamed organoids compared to both non-inflamed CD and controls.  

Key Findings (PIF vs PNI)  
• INNATE IMMUNE SYSTEM (114 genes; DOWN)  
• METABOLISM OF LIPIDS (96 genes; DOWN)  
• INFECTIOUS DISEASE (89 genes; DOWN)  
• CELL CYCLE (79 genes; DOWN)  
• CELLULAR RESPONSES TO STIMULI (77 genes; DOWN)  
• CELLULAR RESPONSES TO STRESS (77 genes; DOWN)  
• NEUTROPHIL DEGRANULATION (74 genes; DOWN)  
• CELL CYCLE, MITOTIC (65 genes; DOWN)  
• SIGNALING BY RECEPTOR TYROSINE KINASES (63 genes; DOWN)  
• AMINO ACID AND DERIVATIVE METABOLISM (44 genes; DOWN)  
…and additional cell-cycle checkpoints, Rho‐GTPase effectors, programmed-cell death, and chemical-stress response pathways all downregulated.

Key Findings (PIF vs Control)  
• METABOLISM OF LIPIDS (92 genes; DOWN)  
• CELLULAR RESPONSES TO STIMULI (74 genes; DOWN)  
• CELLULAR RESPONSES TO STRESS (73 genes; DOWN)  
• NEUTROPHIL DEGRANULATION (64 genes; DOWN)  
• AMINO ACID AND DERIVATIVE METABOLISM (39 genes; DOWN)  
• CELLULAR RESPONSE TO CHEMICAL STRESS (28 genes; DOWN)  
• METABOLISM OF STEROIDS (28 genes; DOWN)  
• rRNA PROCESSING (20–21 genes; DOWN)  
• CHOLESTEROL BIOSYNTHESIS (16 genes; DOWN)  
• CELLULAR RESPONSE TO STARVATION (15 genes; DOWN)  
…and other biosynthetic and replication-related pathways.

Summary  
Across both contrasts, PIF organoids show broad transcriptional suppression of innate immune signaling, metabolic programs (lipid, amino acid, steroid, cholesterol biosynthesis), cell-cycle progression, stress-response modules, and neutrophil-related functions. The largest effect sizes (gene-counts) were seen in innate immunity and lipid metabolism, indicating that inflamed epithelium may be functionally repressed in these core pathways relative to non-inflamed CD and non-IBD controls. The concordance of downregulation across immune, metabolic, and proliferative pathways suggests a global epithelial dysfunction in perianal fistulizing CD.
